papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking the Variational Quantum Eigensolver using different quantum hardware
papers.version_note: arXiv:2305.07092v1 [quant-ph], 11 May 2023; the text layer holds one copy of the paper (6 pages plus an empty trailing page). Figure axes and plot content are not in the text layer; figure and table values are taken from captions, the table text and the surrounding prose.
papers.what_it_is: An empirical comparison of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver on the H2 molecule run on one IBM superconducting processor (ibmq manila) and one AQT trapped-ion processor (aqt marmot), with a fixed ansatz, optimizer and shot count.

existing.note: The iteration counts hold for the stated setup only: nine parameter seeds, 15 iterations per run, 200 shots, the NFT optimizer and no error mitigation. The paper also reports two outlier runs, and the uncertainty bands exclude them.
existing.value: The authors report that, with nine different parameter seeds, 15 iterations per run, 200 shots and no error mitigation, ibmq manila takes an average of 7 iterations to find the ground state, whereas aqt marmot requires approximately 4 iterations.
quotes: We see that the processor ibmq manila takes an average of 7 iterations to
the aqt marmot requires approximately 4 iterations (Figure 6).
This comparison is based upon nine different parameter seeds
Number of shots: 200
Number of iterations: 15
No error mitigation
existing.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on two processors.
existing.reader_inference: The paper does not define how convergence to the ground state is judged, so the iteration counts rest on a reading of Fig. 6 that the text does not specify.

existing.value: The authors state that their results apply only to the two specific processor types and the specific quantum algorithm considered, and cannot directly be generalized to other quantum processors.
quotes: Results reported in this paper exclusivly apply to these two
processor types and the
quantum algorithm considered, and cannot directly be generalized to other quantum processors.
existing.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the scope of its results, Section V.

existing.note: The run times cover 15 iterations of one run and count only the time to evaluate the quantum circuit; the classical parts are excluded. Table II gives an uncertainty for each figure, which the stored value omits.
existing.value: The authors report, for 15 iterations of a run and counting only the time to evaluate the quantum circuit, final energies of −0.975 Ha on ibmq manila and −1.059 Ha on aqt marmot, with quantum run times of 334 and 13297 seconds respectively.
existing.anchor: Table II, text-layer page 4; text on run time, Section III.C
quotes: Time taken (quantum) (seconds) 334 ± 40 13297 ± 625
Over 15 iterations, one run on aqt marmot takes on average 3 hours and 40 minutes
We only consider here the time required to evaluate the quantum circuit, and exclude the classical computation parts.
existing.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on two processors.
existing.reader_inference: The table does not say whether the figures are means over the nine runs; the text says the run time is an average.

assertions.value: The authors state that they chose the two processors because they were easily available to them, and that the IBM Q processor could not be the most recent one because of long queue waiting times.
quotes: The main decisive factor in selecting these two were that they were easily available to us.
prohibitively long waiting times in the queue made extended tests by us impossible
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of how its hardware was selected, Section II.
assertions.reader_inference: The processors are a convenience sample, not a chosen best-in-class pair, which limits what the comparison says about the two hardware technologies.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study concentrates on the H2 molecule and that the work does not include an analysis of the scaling capabilities of the quantum hardware.
assertions.anchor: Section I (Introduction), text-layer page 2; Section IV, text-layer page 5
quotes: we concentrate on simulating the H2 molecule as a basic use case
Our work does not include an analysis of the scaling capabilities of the quantum hardware.
did not delve into evaluating the scalability of the hardware
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit, Sections I and IV.

assertions.value: The authors state that aqt marmot is based on trapped 40Ca+ ions (the text layer prints the superscript flat), supports a register of up to 16 qubits with all-to-all connectivity, and that they use the basis gate set rx, rz and rxx in Qiskit.
assertions.anchor: Section II.A (AQT trapped ion quantum computer), text-layer page 2
quotes: is based on trapped 40Ca+ ions
The aqt marmot system supports a register size of up to 16 qubits featuring all-to-all connectivity.
we choose [rx, rz, rxx] as the basis gate set in Qiskit
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup, Section II.A.

assertions.value: The authors report that aqt marmot has an average single-qubit (rx) gate error of approximately 3 times 10 to the power minus 4 and an average two-qubit (rxx) gate error of around 1 times 10 to the power minus 2, with gate times of 15 µs for single-qubit gates and 200 µs for two-qubit gates, T1 of 1.14 ± 0.06 seconds, T2 of 0.452 ± 0.068 seconds and a coherence to gate time ratio printed as 103 by the text layer, probably ten cubed.
assertions.anchor: Section II.A, text-layer page 2; source cited as [13]
quotes: The error rates of single-qubit gates (rx error) are approximately 3 · 10−4 on average
the error rate of the two-qubit gate (rxx error) is around 1 · 10−2
The typical gate times are 15 µs for single-qubit gates and 200 µs for two-qubit gates.
T1 and T2 times are respectively 1.14 ± 0.06 seconds and 0.452 ± 0.068 seconds
making the coherence/gate time ratio 103 [13]
assertions.certainty_reason: Calibration figures supplied by the vendor and cited to a vendor web page [13]; the paper did not measure them.
assertions.reader_inference: The vendor-supplied figures are used by the authors to explain the run-time gap; they are not checked in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that all runs were made on ibmq manila, a Falcon r.11L processor, with minimal time between runs so that the calibration is similar for each run, and that the average T1 and T2 across the chip are 169 µs and 76 µs.
assertions.anchor: Section II.B (IBM superconducting computer), text-layer page 2
quotes: All runs are performed on the ibmq manila hardware, with minimal time intervals between them, so that the calibration of the hardware is similar for each run.
is a Falcon processor Falcon r.11L version
Average T1 and T2 across the whole chip are 169 µs and 76 µs.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup, Section II.B.

assertions.value: The authors state that other available IBM Q processors feature improved coherence properties but show similar readout (with the exception of ibm sherbrooke), single-gate and double-gate errors.
quotes: Other available IBM Q processors feature improved coherence properties, but show similar readout
(with the exception of ibm sherbrooke), single and double-gate errors
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim without evidence in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that they used the RYCNOT ansatz, a circuit of only four parameterized RY gates and an entangling layer of CNOT gates arranged in a circular manner, because the unitary coupled-cluster (UCCSD) ansatz is unsuitable for benchmarking.
assertions.anchor: Section III.B (Ansatz and Optimizer), Fig. 1, text-layer page 3
quotes: For the purposes of this work, we therefore employed the RYCNOT ansatz.
the circuit is composed of only four RY gates, which are parameterized, and an entangling layer that consists of CNOT gates arranged in a circular manner.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its ansatz, Section III.B.

assertions.value: The authors report that the UCCSD circuit for H2 is already relatively deep, with a circuit depth of 92 for ibmq manila, and state that for more complicated molecules like LiH it becomes impossible to run on real hardware without simplifying the problem.
quotes: For the H2 molecule the circuit is already relatively deep (circuit depth of 92 for ibmq manila)
if moving to more complicated molecules like LiH, it becomes impossible to run on real hardware without simplifying the problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical figure from one transpilation, with the LiH statement an author's claim.
assertions.reader_inference: The depth of 92 is for one transpilation setting that the paper does not describe for UCCSD; the paper states optimization level 3 only for the RYCNOT circuits.

assertions.value: The authors report that, after transpilation with Qiskit optimization level 3, the circuits have similar depth (16 for ibmq manila and 14 for aqt marmot) but differ in the number of 2-qubit gates (8 for ibmq manila and 4 for aqt marmot).
assertions.anchor: Section III.B, Figs. 3 to 5, text-layer page 3
quotes: optimization level 3 is used. Optimization level 3 spends the most computational effort
We see circuits of similar depth (16 for ibmq manila and 14 for aqt marmot)
the number of non-local gates or 2-qubit gates (8 for ibmq manila and 4 for aqt marmot)
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one transpilation of one circuit.
assertions.reader_inference: Gate counts depend on the Qiskit version and the transpiler seed, which the paper does not state.

assertions.value: The authors state that the difference in two-qubit gate count is explained by two swapping operations added for the IBM Q hardware, because SWAP gates are transformed into consecutive CNOT gates and superconducting chips can only directly entangle qubits with a direct connection on the chip.
quotes: This discrepancy can be explained by the addition of two swapping operations for the IBM Q hardware
these chips show a limited
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's explanation of one transpilation result.
assertions.reader_inference: Eight gates against four is consistent with two SWAPs at two CNOTs each, but the paper does not show the transpiled circuit gate by gate in the text.

assertions.value: The authors report that a comparison of the NFT, Nelder-Mead and SPSA optimizers on the qasm simulator suggests NFT outperforms the other two, and that Figure 9 suggests NFT achieves convergence in an average of four iterations on this problem.
assertions.anchor: Section III.B, text-layer page 4; Appendix A, Fig. 9
quotes: Indeed, Figure 9 suggests that NFT achieves convergence in an average of four iterations on this problem.
In the following, we brie
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulator comparison read from a figure.
assertions.reader_inference: The figure values are not in the text layer, so the four-iteration average rests on the authors' reading of Fig. 9.

assertions.value: The authors state that gradient-based methods like Adam perform poorly on such tasks, attributing this to reference [20].
quotes: gradient-based methods like Adam perform poorly on such tasks [20].
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors describe the NFT algorithm as optimizing parameters one at a time by using the sine curve behavior of the loss function for each parameter, and state that it requires two to three evaluations per iteration, based on a hyperparameter.
assertions.anchor: Appendix A (Optimizers), text-layer page 6; method cited as [17]
quotes: The NFT algorithm optimizes parameters one at a time by utilizing the sine curve behavior of the loss function for each parameter.
It requires two to three evaluations per iteration, based on a hyperparameter.
assertions.certainty_reason: A description of a method the paper attributes to other work [17].

assertions.value: The authors state that they simulate H2 with a 4-qubit Hamiltonian in the minimal STO-3g basis set at an interatomic distance of 0.735 Angstrom, with the exact ground state energy EFCI = −1.136189454088 Ha calculated classically.
quotes: For the simulations of the H2 molecule we use the 4-qubit Hamiltonian:
The Hamiltonian is represented using the minimal STO-3g basis set [21].
using prefactors ci at a distance between atoms of 0.735
The exact ground state energy of the problem, calculated classically, is EFCI = −1.136189454088 Ha.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its problem setup, Section III.C.

assertions.value: The authors list the Hamiltonian prefactors, generated with Qiskit's PySCF extension, as c1 = −0.81054, c2 = 0.16614, c3 = 0.16892, c4 = 0.17218, c5 = −0.22573, c6 = 0.12091, c7 = 0.166145 and c8 = 0.04523.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its problem setup, Appendix B.

assertions.value: The authors report that a shot-based simulator (qasm simulator) with the hardware-efficient ansatz reaches an energy error |EVQE−EFCI| of 0.00365 Ha, and they conclude that the ansatz is capable of finding the solution.
quotes: a shot-based simulator (qasm simulator) can achieve relatively accurate energies (|EVQE−EFCI|= 0.00365 Ha)
the ansatz is capable of
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one simulator run.
assertions.reader_inference: A value of 0.00365 Ha is below the chemical accuracy line drawn in the figures only if that line is 0.0016 Ha or larger; the text does not give the line's value.

assertions.value: The authors state that all runs use the RY-CNOT circuit, the NFT optimizer, Qiskit, 200 shots, no error mitigation and 15 iterations.
quotes: Circuit: RY-CNOT (c.f. Figure 1)
Optimizer: NFT
Number of shots: 200
No error mitigation
Number of iterations: 15
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental settings, Section III.C.

assertions.value: The authors state that AQT's hardware currently does not support the native use of error mitigation techniques, so the results for aqt marmot are provided without error mitigation.
quotes: hardware currently does not support the native use of error mitigation techniques.
Therefore, results for aqt marmot are provided without error mitigation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its setup, Section III.C.

assertions.value: The authors report that the choice of parameter seed can impact the optimization process, as seen with two outliers among the nine runs, and that the uncertainty bands, which exclude the outliers, represent one standard deviation from the mean of the seven runs.
quotes: In both cases, the choice of the seed can impact the optimization process, as seen with the two outliers (dotted lines in Figure 6).
These bands in Figure 6, which exclude the outliers, represent one standard deviation from the mean of the seven runs.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The iteration averages of 7 and 4 may or may not include the two outlier runs; the paper does not say.

assertions.value: The authors report a mean energy difference of 0.094 (or 9.34%) between the two processors when considering all runs, and state that the precise reason for this discrepancy in accuracy is not fully understood, as factors such as gate fidelity and connectivity may not fully account for it.
quotes: Moreover, a mean energy difference of 0.094 between the two processors (or 9.34%) is observed when considering all runs
The precise reason for this discrepancy in accuracy is not fully understood, as factors such as gate
and connectivity may not fully account for the observed difference in result precision.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, with the cause left open by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: The text gives no unit for 0.094; Ha is the unit of the surrounding figures. The percentage and the Ha figure agree only if they are taken against a reference near 1.0 Ha.

assertions.value: The authors report minimum energies of −1.006 Ha on ibmq manila and −1.100 Ha on aqt marmot, and absolute errors |EVQE − EFCI| of 0.130 Ha on ibmq manila and 0.036 Ha on aqt marmot.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on two processors.
assertions.reader_inference: In the text layer the second column of the error row sits on its own line; reading it as the aqt marmot value matches the column order of the other rows.

assertions.value: The authors state that Figure 7 and Table II show the energy difference between the last steps of the optimization and the theoretical ground state energy, generated from the last four iterations of the respective hardware runs, and that the unmitigated results are relatively close to the exact ground state.
quotes: Figure 7 and table II show the energy difference between the last steps of the optimization
This plot is generated from the last four iterations of respective hardware runs.
This plot also shows that the unmitigated results are relatively close to the exact ground state.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, read from a figure.
assertions.reader_inference: Table II reports an ibmq manila error of 0.130 Ha, well above chemical accuracy; 'relatively close' is the authors' wording and has no stated threshold.

assertions.value: The authors report that, over 15 iterations, one run on aqt marmot takes on average 3 hours and 40 minutes while ibmq manila takes up to 5 minutes, and state that it is unclear how this run time scales with increasing problem size.
assertions.anchor: Section III.C, Table II, text-layer page 4
quotes: Over 15 iterations, one run on aqt marmot takes on average 3 hours and 40 minutes, while ibmq manila takes up to 5 minutes to get the results (Table II).
It is however unclear how this runtime scales with increasing problem size.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on two processors.
assertions.reader_inference: Table II gives 13297 seconds for aqt marmot, which is about 3 hours 41 minutes and agrees with the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that the zoomed part of the interatomic-distance plot (Fig. 8) corresponds to the global minimum located at 0.735 Angstrom, and that measurement error mitigation on ibmq manila reveals an improvement in accuracy.
quotes: The internuclear distance plot shown in Figure 8 determines the molecular geometry
The zoomed part of the plot corresponds to the global minimum located at 0.735
We also compare here the use of measurement error mitigation for the ibmq manila hardware (green marker), which reveals an improvement in accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, read from a figure.
assertions.reader_inference: The text gives no figure for the size of the improvement; Fig. 8 values are not in the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors state that their results demonstrate that all-to-all connectivity as present in ion trap hardware can significantly decrease the number of non-local gates required, and hypothesize that the optimized energy difference may be due to the impact of SWAP gates (which require 2-qubit gates) on the VQE performance.
quotes: Our results demonstrate that all-to-all connectivity as present in ion trap hardware can
decrease the number of non-local gates required.
We hypothesize that the optimized energy difference may be due to the impact of SWAP gates (which require 2-qubits gates) on the VQE
assertions.certainty_reason: The gate-count reduction is shown for one circuit (8 against 4 two-qubit gates is not quoted here); the link to the energy difference is an author's hypothesis.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper separately says the cause of the accuracy gap is not fully understood, so the SWAP explanation is untested.

assertions.value: The authors state that, based on calibration data, ibmq manila gate times are approximately 103 times (the text layer prints the exponent flat, probably ten cubed) faster than aqt marmot, which results in a difference in quantum run time, and that aqt marmot, with its extended coherence time, can still execute meaningful operations despite slower gate times.
quotes: Based on calibration data, it is known that ibmq manila gate times are approximately 103 times faster than aqt marmot
The aqt marmot backend, with its extended coherence time, can still execute meaningful operations despite having slower gate times.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's statement based on vendor calibration data.
assertions.reader_inference: The ratio of 200 µs to about 300 to 500 ns two-qubit gate times is near 400 to 700, not 1000, so 'approximately 10 cubed' is a rough order of magnitude.

assertions.value: The authors state that the ansatz used is problem-agnostic, so they can anticipate comparable performance for other minimization problems involving a sum of expectation values (such as Ising models).
quotes: The ansatz used is problemagnostic, so we can anticipate comparable performance for other minimization problems involving a sum of expectation values (such as Ising models).
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim without evidence in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: This sits in tension with Section V, which says the results cannot directly be generalized to other processors or algorithms; the Section IV claim is about other problems on the same ansatz, and no such problem was run.

assertions.value: The authors state that increasing the size of the molecule would directly increase the number of qubits required for the simulation, itself linearly increasing the number of SWAP operations required in superconducting hardware.
quotes: increasing the size of the molecule would directly increase the number of qubits required for the simulation, itself linearly increasing the number of SWAP operations
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim without evidence in the paper; the paper states it did not evaluate scalability.

assertions.value: The authors state that they have demonstrated that the VQE serves as a suitable benchmark for evaluating application-centered hardware performance.
quotes: We have demonstrated that the VQE serves as a suitable benchmark for evaluating application-centered hardware performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's conclusion from one experiment on two processors.
assertions.reader_inference: The study gives no analysis of why VQE on H2 would rank hardware in a way that carries to other workloads, and Section V itself denies generalization.

assertions.value: The authors state that the results of this work cannot be used as a recommendation to use one or the other quantum hardware technology, as the results depend on the precise quantum algorithm used and on the precise classical optimizer.
quotes: The results of this work can also not be used as recommendation to use the one or the other quantum hardware technology
and depend on the precise quantum algorithm used, as well as depend on the precise classical optimizer.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limit of its results, Section VI.
assertions.reader_inference: The quote also says the results are processor specific and calibration specific; the words in between are cut at a ligature in the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors state that a practical quantum advantage, an advantage of quantum computation over classical computation in an industrially relevant problem, has not yet been demonstrated.
quotes: A practical quantum advantage, i.e., an advantage of quantum computation over classical computation in an industrially relevant problem has however not yet been demonstrated.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's statement about the field as of 2023, without evidence in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: Time-sensitive: the statement dates from May 2023 and is not checked here against later work.
